Lynne Walz

Democratic candidate for Governor and Lt. Governor, Nebraska · Challenger

Realtor and small business owner; former teacher and former Nebraska state senator

Lynne Walz of Fremont is a Realtor, small business owner, former teacher and former state senator for Nebraska Legislative District 15 (2017–2025). She formed an exploratory committee in November 2025, held a statewide listening tour and announced her campaign for governor on January 21, 2026. She won the Democratic nomination in the May 12, 2026 primary, and her running mate is farmer Ben Steffen.

Where Walz stands

Medical marijuana
Says she would sign an executive order on her first day in office so patients can get medical marijuana with a doctor's prescription. She would also replace Medical Cannabis Commission members who do not carry out the 2024 voter-approved law.
Property taxes
Calls property tax a major affordability issue and links it to the rising age of first-time homebuyers. She says property tax relief should get priority over social issues.
Affordability and child care
Proposes more collaboration and shared resources among local entities to lower costs. One example is businesses opening daycares, or nursing homes and daycares working together.
School choice / vouchers
Says that on her first day as governor she would reject school voucher funds.
Government accountability
Says that on her first day as governor she would hire an independent auditor. She also says state officials should respect ballot measures that voters have passed.
Economy and public schools
Says the governor should focus on creating and attracting good-paying jobs, supporting public schools and lowering the cost of food and other daily expenses.
Transgender student athletes
As a senator, voted against advancing the 2024 Sports and Spaces Act out of the Education Committee. She says the Nebraska School Activities Association already had policies in place, so the Legislature did not need to focus on the issue.
Bipartisanship
Says she will work with people of any party. She cites endorsements from four former Republican legislative colleagues.

Background

  • Nebraska state senator, Legislative District 15 (Fremont area), 2017–2025
  • Democratic nominee for lieutenant governor of Nebraska, 2018
  • Served on the Legislature's Education Committee
  • Realtor and small business owner; former teacher
  • B.A. in elementary education, Midland Lutheran College (1994)
  • Graduated from Arlington High School (1981); born in Fremont, Nebraska
  • Won the 2026 Democratic gubernatorial primary (May 12, 2026)
